test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. - If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. - Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Multi-negative training is a well-supported SASRec ablation. [gSASRec’s IJCAI 2024 summary](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) attributes problems with sampled BCE to overconfidence and combines multiple negatives with generalized BCE; recommended defaults are 128–256 negatives and calibration t=0.75. These results motivate testing broader negative coverage, but do not establish gains on the pinned Amazon benchmark. Electronics’ reported 14.95% negative-outranking rate identifies ranking errors, without proving single-negative training caused them.

Hardness needs controls: [Hard-BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies BPR to reduce false-negative influence during dynamic hard-negative sampling; its evidence concerns implicit collaborative filtering, so SASRec transfer remains experimental. [CATS (2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) studies sequential recommendation directly, using item clustering and adaptive sampling to balance informative negatives against false-negative risk. Neither approach makes unobserved preferences observable; high-scoring unseen items cannot automatically be labeled true negatives.

Practical experiment: compare uniform multi-negative sampled softmax against calibrated multi-negative BCE, then add a modest hard-negative component with a robust loss. Suggested budget-conscious sweep: 16/64/128 negatives, masking padding, positive collisions and known training-history items; compute scores with batched matrix multiplication or chunks on one GPU. These are proposed implementation choices. The [RecSys 2025 LogQ authors’ repository](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) supplies SASRec implementations for uniform, in-batch and mixed sampling, including sampling-probability corrections. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; training margins and published full-catalog results do not establish improvement under 99-negative evaluation.

---

Recent work supports explicitly separating persistent preference from current intent. [TLSTSRec (2024 online; 2025 issue)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) models temporal duration and spectrum, then adaptively fuses long- and short-term sequences. [IBLSRec (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/) uses inferred intent to refine user preferences while separating stable item relationships from transient relationships. For complementary-item discovery, [Fusing temporal and semantic dependencies (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457324002553) separately learns global/local item transitions and stable semantic dependencies; these capture associations, however, rather than establish functional complementarity. Practical inference for this task: combine a full-history encoder with a recent-window encoder through a learned gate conditioned on observed time gaps and representation disagreement. This is a proposed adaptation, not a demonstrated result on the pinned benchmark.

Repeat-consumption research emphasizes timing and context rather than frequency alone. [TSRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531) combines user-specific repeat timing, item-specific intervals, and similarity between current and previous repeat sequences. [MgRIA (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567422326000037) models repurchase intervals as mixtures of decay and periodic peaks. [GDA-REIM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026001838) separates repetition/exploration scoring while suppressing shared attention noise through gated differential attention. Transfer constraint: literal repeat-item scoring cannot help the simulator’s unseen-item recommendations directly. Instead, test whether renewed interest in a historical cluster predicts unseen related items, using histories, timestamps, and available titles/descriptions. Treat recurrence as evidence of latent intent; select architectural changes through macro validation HR@10, without assuming simulator traits are observed.

---

Recent work supports combining sequential collaborative signals with item text, but fusion design matters. [TedRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) argues that directly adding text and ID embeddings can be ineffective; it instead uses Fourier-domain operations for sequence-level fusion. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates BERT representations of titles, descriptions and reviews. Its pretrained encoder and review inputs prevent direct adoption under this benchmark’s constraints. These papers motivate content integration, without establishing gains for a TF-IDF hybrid trained from scratch.

A relevant foundation is [LightFM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.08439): jointly learned metadata-feature embeddings support sparse and cold-start recommendation without requiring pretrained language weights, although the model itself is not sequential. A practical adaptation would encode available titles/descriptions with sparse word and character TF-IDF, then learn a low-dimensional projection alongside SASRec. Alternatively, blend SASRec scores with cosine similarity between candidate text and a recency-weighted history text profile. These are proposed adaptations, not reproduced findings from the cited papers. Separate branches permit testing content contributions before committing to more expensive sequence-level fusion.

For the four-category benchmark, compare ID-only, text-only and hybrid variants using identical validation candidates and macro HR@10. Tune a bounded fusion weight per category before introducing a learned gate based on training interaction counts, history length and text availability. Lexical overlap may distinguish artists, formats and equipment identifiers, but cannot establish compatibility when specifications are absent. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next interaction using item and positional embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward layers. Attention selects relevant past interactions, adapting between recent context and longer histories. Candidate scores use dot products with learned item embeddings. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
